utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-02-54-R77.2, The Prosecutor versus Dusko Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May we have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's Cristina Romano for the Prosecution, and here with me is Milbert Shin and our case manager, Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am attorney Sinisa Simic from Belgrade, and I am here to defend Mr. Dusko Jovanovic, the editor-in-chief of the Montenegrin newspaper DAN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. This Status Conference relates to the forthcoming trial of Dusko Jovanovic for contempt, and its purpose is to make arrangements for that trial. I have a timetable which I will outline, and thereafter I'll ask certain questions from the -- of the Prosecution and the Defence. I have in mind March the 1st for the Prosecution to submit legal submissions, and also to discharge their disclosure obligations under Rule 66 and 68. That will also relate to witnesses. Ms. Romano, how many witnesses do you have?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: At the moment, Your Honour, I think we are calling approximately five witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Five witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: We can review the situation up to the moment we're going to file the 65 ter filings, but at the moment I think we are about five witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Five witnesses, okay. Thank you. Defence submissions to be in by Monday, the 5th of April. And the trial to take place Wednesday, the 12th of May to Friday, the 14th. Mr. Simic, do you have anything to say in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, regarding the dates that you have set, I believe that for now they're absolutely acceptable for us. And as far as Rule 66, I have already received some material from the Prosecution. There are two witnesses who are planned to testify, so we do need to see how much time we need in order to respond to that part. As far as the witnesses that we would like to bring before the Trial Chamber, we would be able to inform you about that at a later date, or we could also give you an estimate. We think that we would be bringing about two witnesses for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we have a possibility of five Prosecution witnesses and two from the Defence, so I think we have more than adequate time. In fact, I think we might be able to complete the trial in two days, but we will maintain the three-day schedule that I have set out. Mr. Jovanovic, stand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there any particular matter that you wish to raise in relation to the trial, or has your attorney spoken for you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the witnesses, I would like to add what I've already stated during an interview to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal, during the interview in Podgorica, and that is that the information about the identity of the protected witness was something that was known to the entire municipality of Plav one day before it was published in the newspaper, and we can bring as many witnesses as the Court believes it requires in order to confirm what I have just stated. I also believe that the protected witness himself would be able to repeat what he has already said during a protected interview for a magazine which is published in Montenegro. It's a weekly magazine in which he confirmed that at the point when he testified, his voice was already recognised in Plav as his, as his authentic voice, and his identity was already known in Plav, it was known that he was the one who was testifying. The other thing I would like to say is that if my previous statement about my guilt or non-guilt has given rise to some uncertainties or unclarified things, I would like to explain it further. I said that I do not deny my objective responsibility as the editor-in-chief of the newspaper. And I take that responsibility, but I do not recognise that there is any subjective responsibility in revealing the identity of the witness or in any subjective responsibility as relating to whether I lied before The Hague Tribunal or not, or that I was in contempt of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: With regard to the first set of matters that you raised, these are issues for your Defence, and those are matters that you will discuss with your lawyer with regard to your Defence. And with regard to the second matter, your plea, it was quite clear that you have pleaded not guilty, so the trial will go ahead. Yes, Mr. Simic. Sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may just add to what Mr. Dusko Jovanovic has just stated, according to the legal system of the former Yugoslavia, or Serbia and Montenegro now, the responsibility for a criminal act besides the state of mind also implies the awareness of the act and the awareness of the consequences. This is what Mr. Jovanovic is speaking about as far as the consequences --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's not pre-empt the Defence that you will make at the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reserve that for the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, Your Honour, there is one question here which needs to be asked, just like the previous question, and that is the jurisdiction of the Court to deal with Mr. Dusko Jovanovic as a person outside the Tribunal who was not in any way a part of the Tribunal who is being charged with a criminal act in relation to the Court. As far as the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, the jurisdiction is laid out in documents of the United Nations, so I don't know whether that can be applied to the acts of Dusko Jovanovic, so I don't know whom we could really apply to in order to resolve this question of jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Romano.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid, but I think that the time for preliminary motions has already passed. The 30-day period has already passed since our last hearing, so if the Defence wants to raise any arguments, I think that the time has already passed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, there is a time for filing preliminary motions, but I don't rule out the possibility of your raising a jurisdictional issue. But strictly speaking, the time has passed. But I don't wish to get into that jurisdictional issue here at all. Is there any other matter that any of the parties wish to raise? Ms. Romano.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Just give me one second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Anything else, Mr. Simic? Anything else relating to the preparations for the trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, last time I asked for all the documents which relate to this case, particularly to the protected witness, to be given to us by the Prosecution. So all the obligations arising from that request as relating to the witness and the accused. However, nobody -- it was not possible to establish, based on the documents from the Prosecution who was in charge of safeguarding the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. identity of the witness, so this is what we would like to have, documents about the duty to safeguard the identity of the witness and whether they related only to the actual witness or whether they also related to third persons as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Romano, have you passed over to the Defence the documents that are required?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: If you can give me another second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not clear exactly he's referring to, but all the material regarding our witnesses will be given during the time period you said about the 65 ter filings. The material that we did referring to the confirming material, I don't know what he's referring to, so unfortunately I don't think I can help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Prosecution asserts that they have passed over to you all the documents that they have. It is for you, Mr. Simic, to manage your case. It may be that you want a document that the Prosecution does not have. In that case, you have to utilise the means that are open to you within the regime that operates here at the Tribunal to get that document. Don't assume that every document that you need for your Defence, the Prosecution has it. But they do assert that they have passed over to you all the documents that related to the indictment. And then you will be receiving on the date or by the date that I have set, March the 1st, their legal submissions as well as the disclosures that they have to make under Rule 66 and 68 relating to witnesses and a summary of their evidence as well as any exculpatory material. It may be that what you have in mind may fall under the latter category, I don't know. But we'll see. If they have not discharged their obligations as they're required to by March the 1st, then you can raise it with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that perhaps the Prosecution did not understand me properly. I am talking about the document based on which the decision is made in which manner a certain witness will be protected. I can stress that in our legal system, there is no such instrument of protection for the witness as is provided in other legal systems, so that I assume that when the Prosecution requested protective measures, had to make a certain security estimate, and on that basis, made the decision how the identity of the witness would be protected in the best way. This is to clarify that matter. As far as our acts are concerned before this Trial Chamber, I can just say that it was quite difficult for us even to come. We just receive a visa for one day, so I cannot address the Court in the proper way in order to have access to certain documents which are perhaps not in the keeping of the Prosecution but they're perhaps with the Trial Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I repeat what I have said: The Prosecution has certain obligations to discharge by March the 1st. If they do not discharge those obligations, then the matter can be taken up with the Trial Chamber. No other matters to be raised? Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but may I be permitted to consult with my attorney? So this is a matter for my Defence, so if I may be permitted just to consult with my attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, but I would like to say one more sentence. We're thinking of the decision whereby Witness K32 was given protective measures. That is the document we are seeking. If that document exists, I would like to see it in order to prepare our position on certain matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You should be able to get that document. Senior legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: To get the document that you have in mind, you should make an application to the Registrar, the Registrar of the Tribunal. There being no other matters, the hearing is adjourned.
